perspective:
**Christian Mensah’s available information / subjective perspective:**

- He knows Jonathan Balogun is his childhood friend and best friend, and someone whose advice he trusts and values.
- Christian had been feeling that Jonathan was hiding something important from him; this made him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- At that meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. Jonathan asked why he thought that and said Christian could trust him.
- Christian told Jonathan he had felt this lately because Jonathan was acting differently. Jonathan admitted he had been hiding something, said he was in trouble, and said he hadn’t known how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic and offered to help Jonathan. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but also said he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian insisted he would help because Jonathan is his best friend.
- Christian suspected the trouble might be related to criminal activity and asked Jonathan if it was illegal.
- Jonathan told Christian he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe and told Jonathan that Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up.
- At that point, Christian said he was not sure yet who was responsible but had some leads. He planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian came to believe/found out that the person behind it was someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both knew and trusted.
- Christian felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and planned to confront the person and bring them to justice.
- Jonathan warned Christian that the person was dangerous, but said he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- Christian’s own actions include: arranging and attending the coffee shop meeting, confronting Jonathan, offering help, asking about illegal involvement, deciding to investigate discreetly, investigating and gathering leads/evidence, telling Jonathan about the framing and the suspected close culprit, and planning to confront the culprit.

**Not available to Christian from the provided dialogue alone:** Jonathan’s private thoughts, any hidden events Christian did not observe or hear about, and the specific name/identity of the culprit beyond Christian’s claim that it is someone close to both of them.
